newsitem.title: CANADA: U.S. can monitor Canada wheat - Goodale spokesman.
newsitem.headline: U.S. can monitor Canada wheat - Goodale spokesman.

text.p: The United States is "absolutely entitled" to monitor Canadian wheat shipments into its market but trade rules do not allow any intervention, a spokesman for Canada's Agriculture Minister said.
"They're absolutely entitled to monitor our wheat shipments but it doesn't change anything," Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale's spokesman Vern Greenshields said.
U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman earlier Wednesday said he was "concerned" about Canadian wheat exports to the U.S. and pledged to monitor the level "very closely."
North Dakota farmers have complained of higher Canadian wheat shipments than usual.
Canada shipped 1.165 million tonnes of all types of wheat to the U.S. from Aug 1, 1996 to Mar 31, 1997, Agriculture Canada said.

Canada agreed to cap wheat and durum wheat shipments to the U.S. at 1.5 million tonnes for the year ended Sept 12, 1995 after it shipped 2.845 million tonnes in the 1993/94 (Aug/July) crop year when flooding in the U.S. played havoc with U.S. crop output.
World Trade Organization agreements since then invalidated the law under which the U.S. restricted Canada wheat imports.
"It's not as high as 1993/94, it's part of the normal ebbs and flows of trade," Greenshields said of recent wheat shipments the U.S. "We imported a large amount of U.S. wheat so far this year."
Canada imported more than three-and-a-half times the amount of U.S. wheat so far this crop year than it did in all of the prior crop year, he added.
The U.S. shipped 95,000 tonnes of wheat to Canada between Aug 1, 1996 and May 13, 1997 compared with 27,000 tonnes in the 1995/96 crop year, Ag Canada said.
"That's the result of Ontario's fusarium problem last year. It's all part of two-way trade," Greenshields said.
Goodale was not available for comment as he campaigned for re-election in his Regina-Wascana constituency in Saskatchewan. Canada's federal election is set for June 2.
